tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='spec/acceptance-criteria.md'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('## Tier 2: concurrency and soft delete')
end=s.index('## Tier 3')
new='''## Tier 2: concurrency and soft delete (draft cards, awaiting ratification)

#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-1: Reads expose the version as a strong ETag
- **Claim.** `GET /notes/{id}`, `POST` (201), `PATCH` (200) and `POST …/restore` (200) return `ETag: "<version>"`, which always equals the body's `version`.
- **Falsifier.** Create a note: `ETag` is `"1"`. Patch it: `ETag` is `"2"`. GET then returns `ETag` `"2"`.

#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-2: Updates require a precondition
- **Claim.** A `PATCH` without `If-Match` gets `428 Precondition Required` and changes nothing.
- **Forbids.** Unconditional updates, which would let lost updates through.
- **Falsifier.** PATCH with no `If-Match` → 428. GET afterwards still shows `version=1` and the old title.

#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-3: A stale writer cannot overwrite a newer version (lost update)
- **Claim.** When `If-Match` doesn't equal the current ETag, `PATCH` gets `412 Precondition Failed`, the note is unchanged, and the response carries the current `ETag`.
- **Forbids.** Two writers holding the same ETag both succeeding.
- **Falsifier.** Alice and Bob both read v1. Alice PATCHes with `If-Match: "1"` → 200, v2. Bob PATCHes with `If-Match: "1"` → 412. GET shows Alice's title at v2.

#### NOTES-FUNC-DEL-1: Delete is soft and idempotent
- **Claim.** `DELETE /notes/{id}` on a live or already-deleted note in the caller's team returns `204`. Afterwards the note is hidden from GET and PATCH (404), but its data is kept.
- **Falsifier.** DELETE → 204, DELETE again → 204, then GET → 404.

#### NOTES-FUNC-DEL-2: Deleted notes can be restored
- **Claim.** `POST /notes/{id}/restore` by a team member returns 200 with the note and increments `version`. GET works again afterwards. Restoring a live note is a no-op 200 that leaves the version unchanged.
- **Forbids.** Non-members restoring (404). Losing content through delete followed by restore.
- **Falsifier.** Create, DELETE, restore → 200 with the same title and body and `version=2`. Carol restoring → 404.

#### NOTES-FUNC-DEL-3: Lists hide deleted notes unless asked
- **Claim.** `GET /teams/{teamId}/notes` excludes deleted notes. With `?archived=true` it lists **only** deleted notes, each with a `deletedAt` value.
- **Falsifier.** A deleted note is absent from the default list and present in `?archived=true`. A live note is the reverse.

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -c '^#### ' spec/acceptance-criteria.md

ratified_on: ""

# Team Notes: acceptance criteria

Status moves from `draft` to `ratified`, and only Patrick ratifies.

The key words MUST, MUST NOT and MAY follow RFC 2119. Aliases follow the pattern `NOTES-<KIND>-<CAT>-<N>`, where KIND is FUNC (behavior), SEC (security) or TECH (technical).

Each card's **Falsifier** is a concrete test that would refute the claim. Each falsifier maps to one or more cases in `conformance/cases.json` through `"falsifies": "<alias>"`.

Shared fixtures (seeded by `spec/schema.sql`):

| User | Token | Teams |
|---|---|---|
| alice | `tok_alice` | `team-red` (owner) |
| bob | `tok_bob` | `team-red` (member) |
| carol | `tok_carol` | `team-blue` (owner) |

---

## Tier 1: MVP, authenticated team notes

#### NOTES-SEC-AUTHN-1: Every endpoint except health requires a valid bearer token
- **Claim.** Requests without `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or with an unknown token, get `401` and a `application/problem+json` body.
- **Binds.** All paths except `GET /health`.
- **Forbids.** Any 2xx response, or any note data, without a valid token.
- **Permits.** `GET /health` → `200` with no token.
- **Falsifier.** `GET /me`, `GET /teams` and `GET /teams/team-red/notes`, each with no token and with `Bearer nope`. Any status other than 401 refutes the claim.

#### NOTES-FUNC-ME-1: `/me` identifies the caller
- **Claim.** `GET /me` returns the caller's `id`, `name`, and the teams they belong to.
- **Falsifier.** As alice, `GET /me` returns `id=alice`, and her teams include `team-red` but not `team-blue`.

#### NOTES-FUNC-TEAM-1: `/teams` lists only the caller's teams
- **Claim.** `GET /teams` returns exactly the teams the caller is a member of.
- **Forbids.** Listing teams the caller does not belong to.
- **Falsifier.** As carol, the list is exactly `[team-blue]`.

#### NOTES-FUNC-NOTE-1: A team member can create a note
- **Claim.** `POST /teams/{teamId}/notes` with a valid `{title, body}` returns `201`, a `Location` header, and the note (`id`, `teamId`, `title`, `body`, `authorId`, `version=1`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`).
- **Falsifier.** As alice, create in `team-red`. The response is 201, `authorId=alice`, `version=1`, and `GET Location` returns the same note.

#### NOTES-FUNC-NOTE-2: Teammates share notes
- **Claim.** Any member of a team can read and list the team's notes.
- **Falsifier.** Alice creates a note, and bob's `GET /notes/{id}` returns 200 with the same content. Bob's `GET /teams/team-red/notes` includes it.

#### NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-1: Non-members cannot see that a note exists
- **Claim.** For a note in a team the caller is not a member of, read, update and delete return `404`, the same as for a note ID that does not exist.
- **Forbids.** `403`, and any body that differs between "exists but hidden" and "does not exist".
- **Falsifier.** Carol sends GET, PATCH and DELETE to alice's team-red note and gets 404 each time. The problem `type`/`title` matches a request for a random UUID.

#### NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-2: Non-members cannot list or create in a team
- **Claim.** `GET` and `POST /teams/{teamId}/notes` for a team the caller is not in, or one that does not exist, return `404`.
- **Falsifier.** Carol lists and creates in `team-red` and gets 404 both times. Afterwards, alice's list does not contain carol's attempted note.

#### NOTES-FUNC-NOTE-3: Members can update a note's title and body
- **Claim.** `PATCH /notes/{id}` with a partial `{title?, body?}` updates only those fields, increments `version`, and refreshes `updatedAt`.
- **Falsifier.** Bob patches the title of alice's note. Afterwards `version=2`, the title has changed, and the body is unchanged.

#### NOTES-FUNC-NOTE-4: Members can delete a note
- **Claim.** `DELETE /notes/{id}` returns `204`. After that, GET returns 404 and the note is no longer in the list.
- **Falsifier.** Delete, then GET → 404, then list → absent.
- *Tier 2 refines this into soft delete with restore (NOTES-FUNC-DEL-\*).*

#### NOTES-FUNC-VALID-1: Input is validated at the boundary
- **Claim.** `title` MUST be a string of 1–200 characters after trimming. `body` MUST be a string of at most 100,000 characters (it defaults to `""`). Unknown fields are rejected. Violations return `422` with a problem body whose `errors[]` names each failing field.
- **Forbids.** Persisting an invalid note, and a `500` for any malformed JSON (which gets `400`).
- **Falsifier.** An empty title, a 201-character title, a title given as a number, an unknown field `foo`, and a malformed JSON body. Each must get 422, or 400 for the bad JSON, and the list must stay unchanged.

#### NOTES-TECH-ERR-1: Errors are RFC 9457 problem details
- **Claim.** Every 4xx/5xx response has `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and a body containing `type`, `title` and `status`, where `status` equals the HTTP status.
- **Falsifier.** Every error case in the suite is checked against the `Problem` schema.

#### NOTES-TECH-CONTRACT-1: Responses match the OpenAPI contract
- **Claim.** Every response body validates against the schema declared in `spec/openapi.yaml` for that operation and status.
- **Falsifier.** The conformance runner validates every response with ajv. Any schema violation fails the run.

---

## Tier 2: concurrency and soft delete (draft cards, awaiting ratification)

#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-1: Reads expose the version as a strong ETag
- **Claim.** `GET /notes/{id}`, `POST` (201), `PATCH` (200) and `POST …/restore` (200) return `ETag: "<version>"`, which always equals the body's `version`.
- **Falsifier.** Create a note: `ETag` is `"1"`. Patch it: `ETag` is `"2"`. GET then returns `ETag` `"2"`.

#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-2: Updates require a precondition
- **Claim.** A `PATCH` without `If-Match` gets `428 Precondition Required` and changes nothing.
- **Forbids.** Unconditional updates, which would let lost updates through.
- **Falsifier.** PATCH with no `If-Match` → 428. GET afterwards still shows `version=1` and the old title.
- *Supersedes Tier 1:* once ratified, the PATCH steps in the NOTES-FUNC-NOTE-3 and NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-1 cases send `If-Match`.

#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-3: A stale writer cannot overwrite a newer version (lost update)
- **Claim.** When `If-Match` doesn't equal the current ETag, `PATCH` gets `412 Precondition Failed`, the note is unchanged, and the response carries the current `ETag`.
- **Forbids.** Two writers holding the same ETag both succeeding.
- **Falsifier.** Alice and Bob both read v1. Alice PATCHes with `If-Match: "1"` → 200, v2. Bob PATCHes with `If-Match: "1"` → 412. GET shows Alice's title at v2.

#### NOTES-FUNC-DEL-1: Delete is soft and idempotent
- **Claim.** `DELETE /notes/{id}` on a live or already-deleted note in the caller's team returns `204`. Afterwards the note is hidden from GET and PATCH (404), but its data is kept.
- **Falsifier.** DELETE → 204, DELETE again → 204, then GET → 404.

#### NOTES-FUNC-DEL-2: Deleted notes can be restored
- **Claim.** `POST /notes/{id}/restore` by a team member returns 200 with the note and increments `version`. GET works again afterwards. Restoring a live note is a no-op 200 that leaves the version unchanged.
- **Forbids.** Non-members restoring (404). Losing content through delete followed by restore.
- **Falsifier.** Create, DELETE, restore → 200 with the same title and body and `version=2`. Carol restoring → 404.

#### NOTES-FUNC-DEL-3: Lists hide deleted notes unless asked
- **Claim.** `GET /teams/{teamId}/notes` excludes deleted notes. With `?archived=true` it lists **only** deleted notes, each with a `deletedAt` value.
- **Falsifier.** A deleted note is absent from the default list and present in `?archived=true`. A live note is the reverse.

## Tier 3: team management and search (outline)
- `NOTES-FUNC-TEAM-2..4`: create a team (the creator becomes its owner). Only the owner can add or remove members. A removed member immediately loses access.
- `NOTES-FUNC-TAG-1`, `NOTES-FUNC-SEARCH-1`: tags are lowercased and capped at 10. `?tag=` filters by tag. `?q=` does a case-insensitive substring search over title and body.
- `NOTES-FUNC-PAGE-1`: `limit` (1–100, default 20) plus an opaque `cursor`. Paging through all pages returns every note exactly once.

77	- **Claim.** Every 4xx/5xx response has `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and a body containing `type`, `title` and `status`, where `status` equals the HTTP status.
78	- **Falsifier.** Every error case in the suite is checked against the `Problem` schema.

80	#### NOTES-TECH-CONTRACT-1: Responses match the OpenAPI contract
81	- **Claim.** Every response body validates against the schema declared in `spec/openapi.yaml` for that operation and status.
82	- **Falsifier.** The conformance runner validates every response with ajv. Any schema violation fails the run.

88	#### NOTES-FUNC-CONC-1: Reads expose the version as a strong ETag
89	- **Claim.** `GET /notes/{id}`, `POST` (201), `PATCH` (200) and `POST …/restore` (200) return `ETag: "<version>"`, which always equals the body's `version`.

93	- **Claim.** A `PATCH` without `If-Match` gets `428 Precondition Required` and changes nothing.

99	- **Claim.** When `If-Match` doesn't equal the current ETag, `PATCH` gets `412 Precondition Failed`, the note is unchanged, and the response carries the current `ETag`.

101	- **Falsifier.** Alice and Bob both read v1. Alice PATCHes with `If-Match: "1"` → 200, v2. Bob PATCHes with `If-Match: "1"` → 412. GET shows Alice's title at v2.

104	- **Claim.** `DELETE /notes/{id}` on a live or already-deleted note in the caller's team returns `204`. Afterwards the note is hidden from GET and PATCH (404), but its data is kept.

options.description: Treat `*` as a version that never matches, so the request fails the precondition check.

# ADR-0002: Concurrency and deletion semantics (Tier 2)

- **Status:** Accepted (decided by Patrick on 2026-10-26; the Tier 2 cards are still awaiting ratification)
- **Builds on:** [ADR-0001](0001-architecture.md), which chose state-based storage with `version`, ETag and `If-Match`
- **Cards:** NOTES-FUNC-CONC-2, NOTES-FUNC-CONC-3, NOTES-FUNC-DEL-2, NOTES-FUNC-DEL-3

## Decision 1: `If-Match: *` is rejected with 428
> In the context of team-shared notes where several members edit the same note, facing the risk that a client sends `If-Match: *` (which RFC 9110 defines as "matches any current representation"), we decided to treat `*` like a missing precondition and answer `428 Precondition Required`, and neglected honoring `*` as an unconditional overwrite or answering 412, to achieve a guarantee that every successful update was made against the exact version the writer saw, accepting a small deviation from the RFC wildcard semantics and no "force overwrite" escape hatch (a client must re-read and retry).

## Decision 2: restore increments `version`
> In the context of soft delete with restore, facing a writer who still holds an ETag from before the note was deleted, we decided that restore is a state change that increments `version` (a no-op restore of a live note does not), and neglected keeping the pre-delete version, to achieve the rule "any state change invalidates old ETags", so stale writers get 412 instead of silently editing a resurrected note, accepting one extra re-read for clients after a restore.

## Decision 3: `?archived=true` is a trash view that lists only deleted notes
> In the context of listing team notes, facing the need to find deleted notes so they can be restored, we decided that `?archived=true` returns only deleted notes, each carrying an optional `deletedAt` that is absent on live notes, and neglected an "include deleted" mixed view, to achieve two simple, disjoint lists (live and trash) that clients don't need to filter, accepting that a combined view needs two requests.

## Consequences
- `Note` gains an optional `deletedAt` field (date-time).
- The PATCH steps in the Tier 1 cases gain `If-Match` once the Tier 2 cards are ratified.
- Falsification faults for Tier 2: `FAULT=ignore-if-match` (lost update), `FAULT=hard-delete`, `FAULT=restore-keeps-version`. Each must turn the suite red on the matching card.
EOF

questions.question: Grok's review asks to pin down several Tier 1 behaviors. The backend already does all of these; we'd only write them into the acceptance criteria and add tests: (a) a non-member's 404 is byte-identical to a missing note's 404; (b) a malformed note id gets the same 404; (c) PATCH with `{}` or `null` gets 422, and every valid PATCH bumps the version; (d) read-only fields like `authorId` in a request body get 422; (e) timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds and a Z, Location is a relative path, and lists return `{items}` newest first. How should we handle them?

options.label: Adopt all as Tier 1 amendment (Recommended)
options.description: These only clarify behavior that already exists. I add the wording and tests and record it as a ratified amendment.

options.label: Adopt, but as Tier 2 cards
options.description: Leave the ratified Tier 1 text as it is and put these in the Tier 2 batch.

options.label: Defer
options.description: Not now. List them under 'what I'd change'.

questions.question: Which error should win when a request has several problems at once? The proposed order: 401 (auth), then 404 (not visible), then 415 (Content-Type isn't JSON), 400 (bad JSON), 413 (too large), 422 (invalid fields), and 428/412 (version check, Tier 2). Today the backend ignores Content-Type, so there is no 415.

options.label: Adopt order, add 415 (Recommended)
options.description: About 5 minutes. A strict media type is easy to defend and makes other-language backends behave the same.

options.label: Adopt order, no 415
options.description: Pin the order down but keep accepting any Content-Type.

questions.question: How should title and body length be counted? This matters for the multi-language rebuilds, because JavaScript, Python, PHP and Rust measure string length differently.

options.label: Unicode code points (Recommended)
options.description: Every language can count these the same way, so an emoji counts as 1. The stored title is trimmed. Node needs a 1-line change.

options.label: UTF-16 code units
options.description: What JavaScript counts by default, so an emoji counts as 2. Other backends would have to imitate it.

options.label: UTF-8 bytes
options.description: Easiest for storage limits, but hard to explain to users.

options.label: Ratify Tier 2 now (Recommended)
options.description: I start building it right away, aiming for Gate 2 around 16:10.

options.label: I'll review first
options.description: I hold Tier 2 and work on Grok's amendments and tests in the meantime.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='spec/acceptance-criteria.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('status: "tier 1 ratified; tier 2 draft"','status: "tiers 1-2 ratified"').replace('ratified_tiers: "1"','ratified_tiers: "1,2"')
s=s.replace("## Tier 2: concurrency and soft delete (draft; decisions folded in 2026-10-26, awaiting ratification)","## Tier 2: concurrency and soft delete (ratified by Patrick, 2026-10-26; supersedes NOTE-3's unconditional PATCH and NOTE-4's delete wording)")
s=s.replace("title MUST be a string of 1–200 characters after trimming. `body` MUST be a string of at most 100,000 characters","title MUST be a string of 1–200 Unicode code points after trimming, and the trimmed value is what gets stored. `body` MUST be a string of at most 100,000 code points")
amend='''
#### NOTES-TECH-ERR-2: Error precedence is fixed (amendment, ratified 2026-10-26)
- **Claim.** When a request has several problems, the first applicable status wins, in this order: `401` (authentication) → `404` (not found or not visible) → `415` (a body is sent and `Content-Type` is not `application/json`) → `413` (body over 2 MiB) → `400` (malformed JSON) → `422` (validation) → `428` (missing or `*` `If-Match`) → `412` (stale `If-Match`).
- **Interface.** 413 comes before 400 because a server must stop reading an oversized body before it can know whether the body parses (ADR-0003).
- **Falsifier.** A non-member sending a `text/plain` malformed body gets 404. A member sending `text/plain` gets 415. A member sending an invalid body without `If-Match` gets 422.

#### NOTES-TECH-FMT-1: Wire formats are pinned (amendment, ratified 2026-10-26)
- **Claim.** Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds and `Z` (`2026-10-26T20:20:43.252Z`). `Location` is a relative path (`/notes/{id}`). Lists are `{"items": [...]}` sorted newest first. Lengths are counted in Unicode code points. A title is stored trimmed.
- **Falsifier.** `createdAt` matches `^\\d{4}-\\d\\d-\\d\\dT\\d\\d:\\d\\d:\\d\\d\\.\\d{3}Z$`. Two notes created in sequence list newest first. A 200-emoji title is accepted and a 201-emoji title is rejected. `"  hi  "` is stored as `"hi"`.

#### NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3: Hidden and malformed ids get the identical 404 (amendment, ratified 2026-10-26)
- **Claim.** The 404 body for a note in another team, for a random UUID, and for a malformed id (`/notes/not-a-uuid`) is byte-identical.
- **Falsifier.** Carol GETs alice's note, a random UUID and `not-a-uuid`. The three response bodies are byte-identical.

#### NOTES-FUNC-VALID-2: Read-only and null bodies are rejected (amendment, ratified 2026-10-26)
- **Claim.** Fields the server owns (`id`, `teamId`, `authorId`, `version`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `deletedAt`) get 422 in POST and PATCH bodies. A body of `null`, `{}` (on PATCH) or a non-object gets 422. Every successful PATCH increments `version` by exactly 1, even if the values are unchanged.
- **Falsifier.** A PATCH with `{"authorId":"carol"}` → 422 with an `errors[]` entry for field `authorId`, and the note is unchanged. A PATCH with `null` → 422. A PATCH with the same title → 200 and version+1.

---
'''
s=s.replace("\n---\n\n## Tier 2", amend+"\n## Tier 2",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -c '^#### ' spec/acceptance-criteria.md; grep -n '^## \|ratified' spec/acceptance-criteria.md | head

# ADR-0003: Error precedence, strict media type, and code-point lengths

- **Status:** Accepted (decided by Patrick on 2026-10-26, from Grok's adversarial AC review)
- **Cards:** NOTES-TECH-ERR-2, NOTES-TECH-FMT-1, NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3, NOTES-FUNC-VALID-2

## Decision 1: one fixed error precedence, with 415 for non-JSON bodies
> In the context of a contract implemented independently in several languages, facing requests that break several rules at once (for example a non-member sending malformed text/plain), we decided on the fixed order 401 → 404 → 415 → 413 → 400 → 422 → 428 → 412 and to reject non-`application/json` bodies with 415, and neglected letting each implementation pick an order or accepting any media type, to achieve byte-for-byte comparable behavior across backends and no information leaks (visibility is decided before anything about the body is revealed), accepting that clients must send the correct `Content-Type`.

*Deviation from the proposed order:* 413 comes before 400, because a server must stop reading an oversized body before it can know whether that body is valid JSON.

## Decision 2: lengths are counted in Unicode code points, and titles are stored trimmed
> In the context of title and body limits enforced by backends in JS, Python, PHP, Rust and others, facing languages that count string length differently (UTF-16 units, bytes, code points), we decided to count Unicode code points and to store the trimmed title, and neglected UTF-16 units and UTF-8 bytes, to achieve one definition every language can implement natively and that matches what users perceive for most text, accepting that grapheme clusters (e.g. family emoji) count as several characters.

## Decision 3: the wire formats are pinned
> In the context of a black-box conformance suite, facing ambiguity in timestamps, Location and list shape, we decided on RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds and `Z`, a relative `Location`, `{items: [...]}` sorted newest first, and byte-identical 404 bodies for hidden, missing and malformed ids, and neglected leaving them to each implementation, to achieve deterministic cross-backend comparison and no existence leaks, accepting a little less freedom in each backend.

## Not adopted
- **405 for unknown verbs:** an unknown method on a known path gets the same 404 as an unknown route, so the API doesn't reveal its route surface. A future card can revisit this.
EOF

input.prompt:
Implement the Tier 2 behavior and the Tier 1 amendments in the reference backend at `~/Projects/project/backends/node-ts`. You wrote the Tier 1 version, so the code will be familiar. Do NOT commit or push, and do NOT edit anything under `spec/` or `conformance/`. If a case looks wrong, report it to me instead.

Read first: `spec/acceptance-criteria.md`, especially NOTES-TECH-ERR-2, NOTES-TECH-FMT-1, NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3, NOTES-FUNC-VALID-2 and the Tier 2 cards CONC-1..3 and DEL-1..3. Also read `spec/openapi.yaml` (v0.2.0), `docs/adr/0002-*.md`, `docs/adr/0003-*.md`, `conformance/cases.json` and `.claude/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`. Follow ub-mode: failing unit test first, pure domain, small changes.

Current state: `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 node conformance/run.mjs --strict` gives 37/45 passing.

Key behaviors:
- **Error precedence, exactly:** 401 → 404 → 415 → 413 → 400 → 422 → 428 → 412.
  - A body-bearing request (POST create, PATCH) whose `Content-Type` media type is not `application/json` (parameters like charset are allowed) gets 415. Check this only after visibility.
  - Restore takes no body, so it gets no 415 check.
- **ETag:** `ETag: "<version>"` on the GET, POST 201, PATCH 200 and restore 200 responses, and on the 412.
- **PATCH preconditions:**
  - Missing `If-Match`, or `*`, gets 428. Check this *after* validation, since 422 wins.
  - A stale value gets 412 with the current ETag.
  - Make the check-and-increment atomic: `UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND version=? AND deleted_at IS NULL`. Zero changed rows means you re-read to decide between 404 and 412.
- **DELETE:** soft and idempotent. A member deleting an already-deleted note gets 204. A non-member, or a nonexistent note, gets 404. A deleted note is 404 for GET and PATCH.
- **`POST /notes/{id}/restore`:**
  - A member restoring a deleted note: clear `deleted_at`, version+1, return 200 with the note and its ETag.
  - Restoring a live note is a no-op 200 with the same version.
  - A non-member gets 404.
- **Lists:** `GET /teams/{id}/notes?archived=true` lists only deleted notes, newest first, each with `deletedAt`. Live notes never include `deletedAt`.
- **Lengths:** counted in Unicode code points (`[...s].length`). The title is stored trimmed.
- **Read-only fields:** `id`, `teamId`, `authorId`, `version`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `deletedAt` in a body get 422 with an error naming that field. A body of `null` gets 422.
- **404 bodies:** byte-identical for hidden, missing and malformed ids. Never include `instance` or `detail` on 404.

**Falsification faults:** these are for proof that the suite catches defects. Implement them through the existing `fault(name)` hook, each one small and clearly commented:
- `FAULT=ignore-if-match`: a PATCH succeeds whatever `If-Match` holds (allows lost updates).
- `FAULT=hard-delete`: DELETE removes the row, so a later restore gets 404.
- `FAULT=restore-keeps-version`: restore doesn't increment the version.
- `FAULT=leak-403`: a non-member gets 403 instead of 404 on GET /notes/{id}.
- `FAULT=no-trim`: the title is stored untrimmed.

Then add `scripts/falsify.sh` at the repo root. For each fault it:
1. Starts the server with `FAULT=<name>` on port 3101 and a fresh in-memory DB.
2. Runs `node conformance/run.mjs --strict` against it.
3. Prints `CAUGHT <fault> by <refuted AC aliases>`, or `MISSED <fault>`.
4. Kills the server.

The script exits non-zero if any fault is MISSED. Use pidfiles and `kill <pid>`, never `pkill -f` with a pattern that could match the calling shell.

**Done when** all of these are green:
- `npm test`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `node conformance/run.mjs --strict`: **45/45**

input.prompt:
Build a performance and correctness benchmark harness for the Team Notes REST service at `~/Projects/project`. Work ONLY in the new directory `bench/`, plus a `Dockerfile` in `backends/node-ts/`. Other agents are editing `backends/node-ts/src` and building `backends/{python,php,deno,rust}` in other worktrees, so don't touch those files. Do NOT commit or push. The time box is about 30 minutes, so aim for a working, simple tool, not a perfect one.

**Context:** read `spec/openapi.yaml` and skim `spec/acceptance-criteria.md`.
- **Seed users and tokens:** alice/`tok_alice` and bob/`tok_bob` on `team-red`, carol/`tok_carol` on `team-blue`.
- **Tier 2 semantics:** responses carry `ETag: "<version>"`. A PATCH needs `If-Match` and gets 412 when stale. DELETE is soft, and `POST /notes/{id}/restore` undoes it.
- **Start commands:**
  - node-ts: `cd backends/node-ts && PORT=… node src/server.ts`
  - Other backends will provide `backends/<b>/run.sh`, which honors `PORT` and `DB_PATH`.

**Deliverables**
1. **`bench/bench.mjs`**: a Node 26 load generator using `fetch` (undici) with zero dependencies.
   - **Usage:** `node bench/bench.mjs --target name=url [--target name2=url2 ...] --runs 3 --duration 5 --concurrency 32 --json bench/results/<ts>.json`
   - **Scenarios, each running for `--duration` seconds at `--concurrency` workers:**
     - `read`: GET /notes/{id} over a pre-created pool of 50 notes.
     - `list`: GET /teams/team-red/notes.
     - `write`: POST new notes.
     - `mixed`: 80% reads and 20% PATCHes. Each PATCH first GETs the note to obtain its ETag. A 412 counts as an expected conflict, not an error.
     - `contention`, the correctness KPI: N workers (default 32) all race PATCHes on ONE note for D seconds. Each worker loops GET → PATCH with If-Match, appending its own marker to the body.
       - Afterwards, check that the final `version` = 1 + the number of 200 PATCH responses. If it doesn't, the difference is the count of **lost updates**.
       - Also report the conflict rate (412s divided by attempts) and the successful-writes/sec.
       - **Lost updates must be 0**, so flag it loudly if not.
     - `authz-under-load`: carol hammers alice's notes, and every response must be a 404. Count any other status as a leak.
   - **KPIs per scenario:** throughput (req/s), latency p50/p95/p99 in ms, error rate (unexpected statuses and network errors), plus scenario-specific values (lost updates, conflict rate, leaks).
   - **Repetition:** run each scenario `--runs` times. Report the mean, stddev and coefficient of variation per KPI, and do a short warmup (1 s) before the measured runs.
   - **Scores:** a composite score per backend.
     - Normalize each throughput KPI to the best backend (best = 100) and each latency KPI inversely.
     - Correctness gates are pass/fail: a backend with lost updates > 0, a leak > 0, or an error rate > 1% gets its score **zeroed**, with the reason shown.
     - Keep the formula simple and print it in the report.
   - **Output:** a markdown matrix (scenario × backend × KPI) to stdout and to `bench/results/latest.md`, and the full raw JSON to `--json`.
2. **`bench/run-local.sh`**: starts the requested backends locally on distinct ports with fresh DBs, waits on `/health`, runs bench.mjs against all of them, then kills them. Use pidfiles and kill by PID only. NEVER use `pkill -f` with a pattern that could match the calling shell.
   - Default to every backend dir that exists under `backends/` and has a known start command.
   - node-ts is the special case. Every other backend uses `backends/<b>/run.sh`.
3. **Docker mode, for standardized and fair resources:**
   - **`backends/node-ts/Dockerfile`**: `node:26-slim`. Copy `spec/` and `backends/node-ts/`, with the build context at the repo root, since `store.ts` loads `../../../spec/schema.sql`. CMD `node src/server.ts` on PORT 3000.
   - **`bench/docker-compose.yml`**: one service per backend, each limited with `cpus: "1.0"` and `mem_limit: 512m`, mapped to host ports 4101+. Include services only for backends that have a Dockerfile, which is node-ts for now. Add commented templates for deno (`denoland/deno`), python (`python:3.14-slim`), php (`php:8.5-cli`, which needs pdo_sqlite) and rust (a multi-stage `rust:1` → `debian:slim` build), with a note that they get enabled once those backends merge.
   - **`bench/run-docker.sh`**: runs `docker compose up -d --build`, waits for health, runs bench.mjs against the mapped ports, then `docker compose down`.
4. **`bench/README.md`**: the KPI definitions, the scoring formula, how to run locally and in Docker, and the caveats: a single machine, the load generator sharing CPU with the servers in local mode, and SQLite write serialization.

**Verification, required:**
- Run `bench/run-local.sh` with node-ts only, using `--runs 2 --duration 3`, and confirm it produces `latest.md`.
- Run `bench/run-docker.sh` for node-ts once with short settings, and confirm it works.
- Note: node-ts is mid-change to Tier 2 by another agent. If PATCH currently doesn't require If-Match, the contention scenario may show lost updates. That is fine; the harness detecting it is a feature, so just report what you saw.

**Report back** in under 200 words: the files, the commands, a sample of the results table, and anything flaky.

input.prompt:
Repo: `~/Projects/project`. Add Dockerfiles so the benchmark can run every backend under identical resource caps.
- **Read first:** `bench/docker-compose.yml`, `bench/run-docker.sh`, `bench/README.md` and `backends/node-ts/Dockerfile` (the pattern to follow: build context at the repo root, copy `spec/` too because backends load `spec/schema.sql` relative to their own folder).
- **Each backend's README and run.sh:** `backends/deno/`, `backends/python/`, `backends/php/`.

**Tasks:**
1. Write `backends/deno/Dockerfile` (`denoland/deno:2.9.x` or a close available tag, with cached deps), `backends/python/Dockerfile` (`python:3.14-slim`) and `backends/php/Dockerfile` (`php:8.5-cli`, confirm pdo_sqlite is present or install it).
   - Each one listens on PORT 3000, with `DB_PATH` set to a file in the container or `:memory:` where that's supported.
   - **PHP:** the built-in server is single-process by default. Set `PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS=4` if the backend still works correctly with it (SQLite file DB). Verify with the conformance suite. If it breaks, use 1 and document why.
2. Enable those services in `bench/docker-compose.yml`, keeping `cpus: "1.0"` and `mem_limit: 512m`, on host ports 4102 (deno), 4103 (php) and 4104 (python). Leave Rust commented out, because another agent is still building it.
3. **Verify:** for each container, run `docker compose -f bench/docker-compose.yml up -d --build <svc>`, then `BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port> node conformance/run.mjs --strict`. It must be 45/45. Then bring it down.
4. Run `bench/run-docker.sh --runs 3 --duration 4 --json evidence/bench.docker.json` across all enabled services, and copy `bench/results/latest.md` to `evidence/bench.docker.md`.

Do not edit any backend source code, `spec/` or `conformance/`. If a backend fails in Docker, report it and don't fix its code. Don't commit, and don't push. Avoid `pkill -f`.

**Report back** in under 200 words: the files, conformance per container, and the bench summary table.

input.prompt:
Repo: `~/Projects/project`. Add Dockerfiles so the benchmark can run every backend under identical resource caps.
- **Read first:** `bench/docker-compose.yml`, `bench/run-docker.sh`, `bench/README.md` and `backends/node-ts/Dockerfile` (the pattern to follow: build context at the repo root, copy `spec/` too because backends load `spec/schema.sql` relative to their own folder).
- **Each backend's README and run.sh:** `backends/deno/`, `backends/python/`, `backends/php/`.

**Tasks:**
1. Write `backends/deno/Dockerfile` (`denoland/deno:2.9.x` or a close available tag, with cached deps), `backends/python/Dockerfile` (`python:3.14-slim`) and `backends/php/Dockerfile` (`php:8.5-cli`, confirm pdo_sqlite is present or install it).
   - Each one listens on PORT 3000, with `DB_PATH` set to a file in the container or `:memory:` where that's supported.
   - **PHP:** the built-in server is single-process by default. Set `PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS=4` if the backend still works correctly with it (SQLite file DB). Verify with the conformance suite. If it breaks, use 1 and document why.
2. Enable those services in `bench/docker-compose.yml`, keeping `cpus: "1.0"` and `mem_limit: 512m`, on host ports 4102 (deno), 4103 (php) and 4104 (python). Leave Rust commented out, because another agent is still building it.
3. **Verify:** for each container, run `docker compose -f bench/docker-compose.yml up -d --build <svc>`, then `BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port> node conformance/run.mjs --strict`. It must be 45/45. Then bring it down.
4. Run `bench/run-docker.sh --runs 3 --duration 4 --json evidence/bench.docker.json` across all enabled services, and copy `bench/results/latest.md` to `evidence/bench.docker.md`.

Do not edit any backend source code, `spec/` or `conformance/`. If a backend fails in Docker, report it and don't fix its code. Don't commit, and don't push. Avoid `pkill -f`.

**Report back** in under 200 words: the files, conformance per container, and the bench summary table.

M	bench/docker-compose.yml
# Seven decisions for Patrick (proposed cases: adversarial.cases.json)
Every case has `"status": "proposed"`. The runner has no status convention, so these live in a separate file and cannot affect the ratified suite.

**a. If-Match with a weak tag or a list.** Options: weak `W/"1"` → 412 (node: any non-`"n"` value is treated as stale; RFC 9110 says If-Match uses strong comparison) or → 200 if weak matches. A list `"9", "1"` → 200 if any tag matches (deno, php and python split on commas; node returns 412 for any list). `"1", *` → 428 or 412. **Recommendation:** weak → 412, a list matches if any member matches, and a list containing `*` → 428. That follows RFC 9110 and keeps CONC-2's no-wildcard rule.

**b. `?archived=` with yes, 1, empty or TRUE.** Options: 422 naming `archived` (the spec enum is `['true','false']`), 400, or treat anything that isn't `true` as false (what all four backends do now, giving 200 with live notes). **Recommendation:** 422 with `errors[].field = "archived"`, because the spec's enum already says other values are invalid. This needs a 422 response added to `listNotes` in openapi.yaml.

**c. An empty body on POST/PATCH.** Options: 400 (empty isn't JSON), 415 (no Content-Type), or 422. ERR-2 says 415 applies only when "a body is sent", so a zero-length body skips 415 and fails parsing. **Recommendation:** 400 whatever the Content-Type is, since that is the literal reading of ERR-2 and it is what the rebuilds converged on.

**d. An unknown route with no token.** Options: 401 (ERR-2 puts 401 first, and AUTHN-1 binds "all paths except health") or 404 (most routers 404 before auth middleware runs). **Recommendation:** 401. It's the literal reading and doesn't reveal the route surface. With a token, an unknown route or verb → 404 (ADR-0003 "Not adopted": no 405).

**e. Does DELETE bump version, ETag or updatedAt?** Options: DELETE leaves version alone and only restore bumps it, or DELETE bumps too. **Recommendation:** DELETE and a repeated DELETE don't change version. Restore from deleted → version+1 and `ETag "2"`, and restoring a live note changes nothing. DEL-2 already implies this, since restore's bump exists to invalidate pre-delete ETags. Still open: should DELETE set updatedAt? I propose no, with only `deletedAt` set. There's no case for that yet.

**f. `errors[].field` for a non-object body.** Options: `"$"` (node-ts, python; JSONPath root, RFC 9535), `"(body)"` (deno, php), or omit `errors[]`. **Recommendation:** `"$"`. It's a real standard, and it already splits 2–2, so one choice has to win.

**g. Trimming and code points.** Options: Unicode White_Space (JS `trim()` and Python `str.strip()` both strip NBSP, U+2003, U+3000, tab and newline) or ASCII-only (PHP `trim()`, which leaves NBSP). No language trims U+200B, since it isn't White_Space. **Recommendation:** strip Unicode White_Space, keep U+200B as a real character (so a title of just ZWSP is valid), and count code points (`é` written as e+U+0301 counts 2, and a ZWJ family emoji counts 5). PHP must use `preg_replace('/^\s+|\s+$/u', …)`.
# Adversarial cases: results on the four backends

Run on main at the time of writing. All four backends pass the ratified suite (45/45, 22/22 ACs). These 29 cases are proposed, not ratified; the expected values are the reviewer's recommendation, so a failure marks a place where the backends disagree with that recommendation, not a bug. Each decision belongs to Patrick. See `questions.md`.

Run: `CASES=conformance/adversarial.cases.json BASE_URL=http://localhost:PORT node conformance/adversarial-run.mjs`

| Backend | Passed | Failing groups |
|---|---|---|
| node-ts | 18/29 | If-Match list containing the current tag, list with `*`, `?archived=` bad values (4), empty body (3), unknown route without a token (2) |
| deno | 20/29 | list with `*`, `?archived=` bad values (4), `errors[].field` for non-object bodies (4) |
| php | 20/29 | list with `*`, `?archived=` bad values (4), `errors[].field` for non-object bodies (4) |
| python | 25/29 | `?archived=` bad values (4) |

Whitespace trimming and code-point counting (question g) pass on all four. Verdicts come from the runner, not from Grok.

questions.question: Grok's PR #72 lists 7 places where the rebuilds disagreed. Four are uncontroversial. Accept Grok's recommendation for all four? (c) An empty body gets 400. (e) DELETE changes neither `version` nor `updatedAt`; only restore bumps the version. (f) `errors[].field` is `"$"` (the JSONPath root) for a body that isn't an object. (g) Trimming strips Unicode whitespace, a zero-width space counts as a real character, and lengths are counted in code points.

options.label: Accept all four (Recommended)
options.description: These follow existing cards, the RFCs, or what most backends already do. Each becomes ratified wording plus test cases.

options.label: Accept, except (f)
options.description: Keep the field name implementation-defined. Tests would check only that `errors[]` exists.

options.label: Defer all to 'next'
options.description: Leave them unspecified and record them as known gaps.

questions.question: (a) What should PATCH do with a weak ETag (`W/"1"`) or a list (`"9", "1"`) in `If-Match`?

options.label: RFC 9110 strong match (Recommended)
options.description: A weak tag gets 412. A list matches if any entry matches. A list containing `*` gets 428, keeping the no-wildcard rule. Node changes; Python already does this.

options.label: Single tag only
options.description: Anything other than exactly one `"N"` gets 412. Simpler, but it breaks the HTTP standard for lists.

questions.question: (b) What should `?archived=` do with values other than `true` or `false` (`yes`, `1`, empty)?

options.label: 422 naming archived (Recommended)
options.description: The OpenAPI enum already says these are invalid. All 5 backends need a small change, and the spec gains a 422 response.

options.label: Treat as false
options.description: Loosen the spec to match what all 5 backends already do: anything other than `true` shows the live list. No code changes.

questions.question: (d) An unknown route with no token: 401 or 404?

options.label: 401 (Recommended)
options.description: The literal reading of the error-order card: authentication comes first. An unauthenticated caller learns nothing about which routes exist. Node and Deno change.
What most routers do. Requires amending NOTES-SEC-AUTHN-1 so it applies only to known routes.
