A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme: then omit the media query and `[data-theme]` blocks entirely but still set the background and every color explicitly, so the page looks right on either host background; do this by choice, never by omission.

**Use layout for spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap` instead of per-element margins, which collapse or double without warning. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width, written `padding-left: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px))` and `padding-right: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px))` so that it also clears a system bar at the phone's side: set it once on `body` or one outer wrapper (where colored bands span the width, on each band's inner wrapper), whose vertical padding uses `padding-block` and never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (about 400px). Give images and any `aspect-ratio` box `max-width: 100%`, and don't give anything a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only wide tables, code, and diagrams may exceed it; give each `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. The publish skeleton pads `:root` top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets (zero everywhere except a phone app) so the page runs edge to edge while its content stays clear of the system bars; keep that padding. Put `<meta name="claude:viewport-fit-sides" content="cover">` at the top of the file beside your `<title>`: it promises that the side gutter uses those two `max()` paddings, so the tag goes in only together with both paddings, never alone. An edit of an older page that has neither leaves both out, unless the ask redoes the page's layout. With it the page also runs under a system bar at the phone's side. Anything fixed to a screen edge stays at `0` and adds that edge's inset to its own padding (one that spans the width takes the side gutter too); a floating or absolutely placed control adds the nearby edges' insets to its offsets. A sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` and never `0`. So that nothing scrolls into view above it, under the host's controls, paint that band with `body::before { content: ""; position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto; height: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px); z-index: 10; background: ... }`, in the header's own background where the header opens the page and in the page's where the sticky bar starts lower. Size a one-screen app with `height: 100%` on `html` and `body` instead of `100vh`, so it fits inside the `:root` padding. A page that includes its own viewport meta gets the `:root` padding only when that meta declares `viewport-fit=cover`. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Make repeated elements consistent.** For cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, or badges on sibling items, use the same edges, baselines, and inner padding on each, and put any recurring element in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over empty space or sits alone in a row. Make text that can outgrow its track wrap or scroll in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Use card styling selectively.** Border, fill, radius, and shadow each mark an element as a separate object. Apply them by role, to set off the one element that needs it; applying the same radius and shadow to every block flattens the hierarchy. Open with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to scale.** Place marks, ticks, and labels with one scale, and make every label name a value the chart actually reaches. Color chart text from the theme tokens so it is readable in both themes. Keep marks, labels, and edges clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds; in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Make the page complete at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, with no scrolling to trigger it; that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all see. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never left at `opacity: 0` waiting for an observer. Size a hero to its content instead of to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the rest of the page out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state: the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, or a plausibly filled form, clearly marked as examples and never presented as the user's own figures. The first view shows what the tool does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing. When those records live in the `db` capability, keep them out of the page source. Its first frame renders before the store answers, so make that frame a designed empty state that names what will appear and how to add the first entry, then fill it from the store. Seed the store through the `ArtifactData` tool (what type instructions call `write_db`) after the first publish: the user's real data, or marked examples for a tool only the user will use. For a store other people will fill with their own entries, seed only what the user gave you or asked for, never invented people or records.

**Avoid AI-generated design.** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. When the user specifies a visual direction, follow it exactly; their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. When nothing is specified, don't use that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly.** Watch for overlapping elements, cascade collisions, and silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform preserves form values, focus, and scroll position across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, use Canvas or WebGL instead of hand-writing long SVG path data.

**CSS rules.** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificity. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out, e.g. a type-based selector like `.section` and an element-based one like `.cta` both setting padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't undo your spacing unnoticed.

**Writing the copy.** Treat words as design material and never as decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen: name things by what people recognize instead of how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*; they don't manage *webhook config*). Use active voice; a control states exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologies or vagueness. Prefer specific to clever. Write plainly, the way a knowledgeable person would talk. Avoid mannered devices: asides set off by em-dashes, "not X, but Y" framing, colon-then-reveal sentences, scare quotes around invented labels, and stock phrases such as "worth noting" or "honest caveat". Prefer short, direct sentences over compressed or clever phrasing.

**Name the page like a product; don't caption it.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it gives the reader a first impression of the care taken. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject; or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which then is the page's name. When the user already has a specific name for the thing, use that name for the title rather than coining a new one. Stop at the name; a title that adds its own explanation after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it appears beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could apply to any of them fails as a name just as an appended explanation does. When a candidate title combines the name with a generic word (a greeting, a category, a page-type label), keep the name; a trim that drops the identifying part and keeps the generic word produces a title that could apply to any page. This rule removes explanations and doesn't require brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. Put the explanation in the one-sentence publish `description`; the gallery shows it directly under the title.

**Structure is information.** Structural devices (numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels) should encode something true about the content instead of decorating it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but those fit only if the content actually is a sequence, such as a real process or a typed timeline where the order is information the reader needs. Before adding numbered markers or similar devices, check that they actually make sense.

**When the page is a UI (dashboard, tool).** It is scanned and operated instead of read top to bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Put the summary before the detail. Encode state in form as well as in numbers (a pill, a chip, a severity stripe) so that whatever needs attention is visible at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. Interactive elements should look interactive.



## Process

Start from what the viewer should be able to do on the page, in addition to what they will read. If the page should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user. A page that is only read doesn't need that.

Before writing the page, settle a short design plan (a compact token system) and write it into the file itself, as the `:root` block at the top of the page's `<style>`, rather than into your reply:
- **Color**: the palette as 4-6 named color tokens.
- **Type**: font tokens for 2+ roles: a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: the layout concept as a one-line comment above the tokens.

Then build the rest of the page from those tokens, deriving every color and type decision from them. The plan is working material, not part of the answer: unless the user asks about the design, one plain sentence on the direction is the most to say about it, with no hex values or font names.

**Write, check once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once, where this session offers a way: one `ArtifactCheck` preview (or the Artifact tool's own `action: "preview"` where there is no separate `ArtifactCheck` tool), or else one screenshot of the local file; if the session offers none of these, skip the look. The preview renders desktop and phone widths in light and dark and lists overflow, colors that ignore the theme, blocked loads and console errors, including a script that fails to parse, so nothing it covers needs a check of your own. The look is optional: if you take it, make one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look; then publish. For a page that charts real numbers, take the look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. A page whose point is logic (dates, money, scoring, parsing) may get one more check before publishing: one run of a pure function on a sample input, or, where no preview ran, one syntax check of its script; nothing more. A page that declares `capabilities` takes the look rather than skipping it, then one functional pass after the first publish, because the preview cannot run that code: read back once what the page stores or serves (one read of its stored data or one read-only route call; where that read alone would prove nothing, as on an empty store, you may first write one probe document yourself and delete it after the read, passing the `version` the write returned as `if_version`; no other test writes unless the user wants one), tell the user in one line what you exercised and what you could not, and stop. None of this becomes a loop, because the user is waiting for a link: no second screenshot, no scripts that probe the DOM, no re-running a check that passed. Review happens on the live page, and further polish is for the user to request; if the user reports something visibly broken (a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing), fix that, take at most one more look if the session offers a way, and republish once. These checks are for code you wrote into this page, not for content you fill into an Artifact made from an Artifact type (a Slides deck, a Design canvas): there the type's own instructions say whether to check, and if they say nothing, don't.

**Open viewers.** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open: published changes are delivered to them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state preserved where possible. If your page has state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`; `hot` is the viewer's own update hook, not a capability behind `claude.use()`, and is absent outside a viewer, hence the `?.`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance changes here: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated decisions, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part in the plan itself, without narrating the revision to the user. Write the code only after the plan is specific to this subject, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero states the thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (headline, image, live demo, interactive moment). 
- Typography sets the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, avoiding the families you would use on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design instead of a neutral container for the content. 
- Use motion deliberately. Think about whether and where animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. One orchestrated moment is usually more effective than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation adds to the impression that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Put your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent clashes with the background, shift it toward an analogous hue or desaturate it instead of replacing it.

On this page ModelVisibilityConcurrencyDelete & restoreErrorsTeamsImplementations

Team Notes Service

A REST backend where small teams share notes. Every member of a team can read and edit its notes. Outsiders can't tell that a note exists, and two people editing at once can't silently overwrite each other.

The model

There are three things: users, teams and notes. A user belongs to teams as an owner or a member. A note belongs to exactly one team, keeps its author, and carries a version that goes up by one on every change.

Visibility: one 404 for everything you can't see

A note in someone else's team, a note that never existed, a malformed id, a deleted note and an unknown route all return the same bytes, a 404 problem document. A curious user learns nothing by probing ids. The one 403 in the API goes to a team member who isn't the owner and tries to change membership, because they can already see the team.

Carol asks for…StatusBody
Alice's note in team-red404identical
A random UUID404identical
/notes/%E0 or /notes/{id}/404identical
Anything, with no token401Authentication comes before routing

Concurrency: no lost updates

Every read returns ETag: "<version>". To edit, you send it back in If-Match. The server checks and increments in one statement, UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND version = ?. If someone else got there first, you get 412 and the current ETag, so you can re-read and retry. With no precondition at all you get 428: unconditional overwrites aren't allowed.

Delete and restore

DELETE is a soft delete. It's idempotent, keeps the content, and leaves the version alone. POST /notes/{id}/restore brings the note back and bumps the version, so anyone still holding a version from before the delete gets 412 instead of quietly editing a resurrected note. ?archived=true lists the team's trash.

Errors and their order

Every error is an RFC 9457 application/problem+json document. When a request breaks several rules at once, the first one in this chain wins, in every implementation:

401→404→415→413→400→422→428→412

Authentication → visibility → media type → size → JSON syntax → validation → precondition → version. Visibility is decided before anything about the body is revealed.

Teams

Anyone can create a team with a readable slug and becomes its owner. Only the owner adds or removes members. Access follows membership immediately: a removed member gets the same 404 on their very next request, even for notes they wrote. Those notes stay with the team. The last owner can't leave, so no team is ever left without an administrator.

Five implementations, one contract

questions.question: Where does 403 go in the error order? Today's order is 401 → 404 → 415 → 413 → 400 → 422 → 428 → 412, and 403 only happens on membership changes by a member who isn't the owner. Node and Rust independently chose 404 → 403 → 415 → 422. Python, Deno and PHP aren't tested on this yet. The real question is whether a forbidden caller ever learns anything about their request body.

options.label: A: 401→404→403→415→413→400→422→409 (Recommended)
options.description: Permission is checked before the body is even read, so a non-owner never sees media-type or validation feedback. It's also cheapest: forbidden requests are rejected without reading the body. This matches what Node and Rust do. 409 (taken slug, last owner) comes last, because a state conflict only makes sense for valid input.

options.label: B: 403 after validation (…→422→403)
options.description: Validate first and authorize last, as some frameworks do by default. It reveals validation rules to people who can't act, and it means reading and parsing bodies of requests you'll reject anyway. Not recommended.

options.label: C: like A, but 409 before 422
options.description: Same as A, except the conflict check (taken slug) comes before field validation. Gives a 409 for a taken slug even when other fields are invalid. Arguable, but it inverts 'valid input first', so A is cleaner.

- **Claim.** `title` and `body` must be sequences of Unicode scalar values. A lone surrogate escape such as `"\\ud800"` gets 422 naming the field, because it can't be stored and read back unchanged. The limits are inclusive: a body of exactly 100,000 code points is accepted and 100,001 is rejected.

#### NOTES-SEC-AUTHN-3: Malformed paths never produce 5xx (from red team, 2026-10-26)
- **Claim.** Any request path, including `//`, `///notes`, `/./` or percent-junk, gets 401 without a token and the identical 404 with one. It never gets a 5xx.
- **Origin.** The red-team fuzzer (invariant I1) found `GET //` and `POST //` returning 500 on node-ts.

'''

Here is the brief, with tradeoffs and my recommendation for each. Claude's screen shows it already asked you about restore and stray bodies, and recommended a uniform 415, so you may have answered that part. Any of these can go to Claude's question tool if you prefer.

a. If-Match forms (weak tag, list, *).

Option 1, strict (recommended): a weak tag gets 412, a list matches if any tag matches, and a list with * gets 428. It follows RFC 9110, and the cost is a small parser in each backend.
Option 2, simple: only a single strong tag is supported, and anything else gets 412. It is cheapest, and it matches what node-ts does today, but clients that send lists fail.

content.thinking: This new case reveals four distinct behaviors across five languages for a lone surrogate in JSON: Node stores it corrupted, Deno replaces it with U+FFFD, PHP/Rust reject it with 400, and Python rejects it with 422. This is exactly the kind of divergence worth flagging, so I need your input on how to handle it.

questions.question: A JSON string containing a lone surrogate (`"\ud800"`): which status should it get? JSON (RFC 8259) technically allows the escape, but I-JSON (RFC 7493) forbids it, and it can't be stored as UTF-8 without changing it. Today Node stores it corrupted, Deno silently changes it, PHP and Rust return 400, and Python returns 422.

# Team Notes red-team findings (2026-10-26, 15:53–15:59 CDT)

Black-box HTTP probes against the four backends, aimed by reading the source. Ports: 4201 node-ts, 4202 deno, 4203 php, 4204 python. Each backend used a throwaway DB under `/tmp` (`/tmp/rt-*.db`). No repo files were changed.

Scripts in this directory:
- `probe.mjs` is the raw-socket sweep (paths, headers, JSON, If-Match, leaks, framing). Its output is in `results.txt`, and `compare.mjs` writes the side-by-side view to `compare.txt`.
- `probe2.mjs` covers persistence, 20-way races, pipelining and timing (`results2.txt`). `timing.mjs` is the 1,500-sample timing run (`timing.txt`).
- `size.sh` covers the 2 MiB boundary, `deno-nul.sh` the NUL truncation, and `rawsend.mjs` is a raw TCP sender.
- `repro.sh` re-runs every top finding as an exact curl or raw request. Its output is in `repro.txt`.

Severity: **blocker** breaks a ratified card or loses data, **should-fix** is a real defect or a spec gap that lets backends diverge, and **nit** is cosmetic or low impact.

## Findings

| # | Backend | Probe (exact) | Expected per spec | Actual | Severity | Differs across backends? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | node-ts, deno | `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_alice' localhost:PORT/notes/%E0` (also `%C0%AE`, `/notes/%`, `/teams/%E0/notes`, PATCH, DELETE, `POST /notes/%E0/restore`) | 404, byte-identical to the 404 for a random UUID (NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3, malformed id) | **500** problem+json. `decodeURIComponent` throws on an invalid escape (node `http.ts:78`, deno `http.ts:89,104`). | **blocker** | yes: php and python return 404 |
| 1b | node-ts | `curl localhost:4201/notes/%E0` (no token) | 401 (401 comes first in NOTES-TECH-ERR-2) | **500**. Path decoding runs before authentication. | **blocker** | yes: deno, php and python return 401 |
| 2 | deno | `./deno-nul.sh 4202`: POST `{"title":"\u0000","body":"keep\u0000secret-tail"}` | 201 storing the strings as sent (as node, php and python do), or 422 | 201, then GET returns `"title":""` and `"body":"keep"`. Everything after U+0000 is **silently truncated**, so an empty title (minLength 1) gets persisted. The list responses then break NOTES-TECH-CONTRACT-1. | **blocker** (data loss and contract violation) | yes |
| 3 | node-ts, deno | `printf '{"title":"a\xff\xfe"}' \| curl -X POST .../teams/team-red/notes -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @-` and `-d '{"title":"\ud800x"}'` | 400, because invalid UTF-8 is malformed JSON (RFC 8259). At minimum the stored value must match the response. | 201. Invalid bytes are replaced with U+FFFD and stored. For a lone surrogate, **node's 201 body says `"\ud800x"` but a later GET returns `"�x"`**, under the same ETag `"1"`. | should-fix | yes: php 400/400, python 400/422 |
| 4 | all | PATCH with `If-Match: "1", "2"`, `If-Match: "1", *` or `If-Match: "01"` on a v1 note, and duplicate `If-Match` headers (`"9"` then `"1"`) | Not pinned beyond "missing or `*` gets 428, stale gets 412" (NOTES-FUNC-CONC-2/3). RFC 9110 says a list matches if any member matches, and the strong comparison is octet-exact, so `"01"` ≠ `"1"`. | **node**: every list gets 412, and `"01"` gets **200** (the regex is numeric). **deno, php**: `"1", *` gets 200 and duplicate headers are joined. **python**: `"1", *` gets 428, and for duplicate headers the first one wins (412). | should-fix (add an AC card) | yes, four different behaviors |
| 5 | deno (php weaker) | `node timing.mjs 4202`: carol GETs alice's note (99 KB body), a random UUID and `zz`, 1,500 samples each in random order | No existence leak through status, body, headers **or timing** (ADR-0001) | deno: hidden p25 108 µs / p50 137 µs vs random 79 / 101 µs, so a non-member's 404 is about **30 µs slower** when the note exists. `findNote` loads the whole row and then `isMember` runs. php: about 25 µs slower (710 vs 687 µs). node-ts: no gap (it uses one JOIN). Python's 40 ms keep-alive delay (#7) hides any gap. | should-fix | yes |
| 6 | python | `printf 'GET /health HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: -1\r\n\r\n' \| node rawsend.mjs 4204 3000` | 400 | **Hangs**. `rfile.read(-1)` blocks the worker thread until the client closes, so one client can pin unbounded threads. `Content-Length: abc` or `1e1` closes the connection with no response. | should-fix (DoS) | yes: node and deno answer 400 |
| 6b | python | chunked body with size line `zz` (see `repro.sh` F14) | 400 | **500** (`int('zz',16)` raises ValueError) | should-fix | yes: node 400, deno and php drop the connection |
| 6c | python, php | `Content-Length: 13` and `Content-Length: 14` (python), or `Content-Length: 4` plus `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (python and php) | 400. RFC 9112 forbids these, and they enable request smuggling behind a proxy. | 201. Python uses the first CL or the chunked body, php the chunked body. | should-fix | yes: node and deno answer 400 |
| 7 | python | `curl -s -o /dev/null -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' localhost:4204/health localhost:4204/health` | Comparable latency | First request 1.7 ms, then **40 ms per request** on a keep-alive connection. Headers and body go out in separate small writes, so Nagle's algorithm meets delayed ACKs. Every keep-alive client (fetch/undici, browsers) pays this. | should-fix (perf) | yes |
| 8 | php | `printf 'GET /health ...\r\n\r\nGET /health ...\r\n\r\n' \| node rawsend.mjs 4203 3000` | Two responses (or one plus `Connection: close`) | **No response at all**: pipelined requests are dropped by `php -S`. Malformed framing (`CL: abc`, `-1`, a path without a leading slash) also closes with no response, and duplicate CL hangs for more than 4 s. | should-fix (`php -S` is a dev server) | yes |
| 9 | node-ts | `curl localhost:4201/nope`, `curl -I localhost:4201/health`, `OPTIONS *` (no token) | NOTES-SEC-AUTHN-1 binds "all paths except `GET /health`", so 401. ADR-0003 says an unknown route gets the same 404 as a missing one. The two rules conflict for unauthenticated requests. | node: **404** (route check before auth), and `GET /health/` returns 200. Others: 401. | should-fix (pin in an AC) | yes |
| 10 | node-ts, deno vs php, python | `curl -X POST .../teams/team-red/notes -H "$A"` (no body, no Content-Type). `PATCH` with `Content-Type: text/plain` and `Content-Length: 0`. | NOTES-TECH-ERR-2: 415 only when "a body is sent". With no body the request is malformed, so 400. | node: 415 in both cases. deno: 415 for the first and 400 for the second. php and python: 400 in both. | should-fix | yes |
| 11 | all | Title made only of `\u001f`, `\u0085`, `\u180e` or `\ufeff` | "Trimmed" (NOTES-TECH-FMT-1) with one definition across backends (ADR-0003) | U+001F: python trims (422), the rest store it. U+0085: php and python trim (422), node and deno store it. U+180E: only php trims. U+FEFF: python **stores a BOM-only title**, the rest trim it (422). | should-fix (pin the whitespace set) | yes |
| 12 | all | `GET /teams/team-red/notes?archived=true&archived=false` and the reverse order | One defined behavior | node and deno use the first value, php and python the last, so the same URL returns trash on two backends and live notes on the other two. | nit | yes |
| 13 | all | `/teams/team-red/notes/`, `/me/`, `/notes/{id}/`, `/teams/team%2Dred/notes`, `/x/../me`, `/x/%2e%2e/me`, `//me` | Exact paths only (OpenAPI) | Trailing slash: node and php return 200, deno and python 404 (`/me/` and `/teams/` return 200 only on node). `%2D` gets 404 on python, which never percent-decodes, and 200 elsewhere. Dot segments: node and deno resolve them to 200. `//me` and `//teams/team-red/notes` return 200 only on python. | nit | yes |
| 14 | python, php | `{"title":99…9}` (5,000 digits). `{"title":"x","z":[[[…600 deep…]]]}`. `{"title":"x","\u0000a":1}`. | 422, because the JSON is well-formed but invalid | python returns **400** for the huge int (int max-str-digits limit). php returns **400** for nesting deeper than 512 and for a NUL-prefixed key. | nit | yes |
| 15 | deno | POST with a UTF-8 BOM before `{"title":"x"}` | 400 (malformed JSON, as on the other three) | 201 (TextDecoder strips the BOM) | nit | yes |
| 16 | all | `GET /me` with two `Authorization` headers (carol's, then alice's) | 401, or one defined behavior | node and python authenticate as the **first** token (carol). deno and php return 401. | nit | yes |
| 17 | php, python | Response headers on any request; `DELETE` 204 | No version disclosure; a 204 has no Content-Type | php sends `X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.12` and `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8` on the 204. python sends `Server: TeamNotesPy Python/3.14.8`. | nit | yes |
| 18 | all | Any 404/422 compared across backends | Problem bodies are pinned only within a backend (NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3) | `type` and `title` differ by backend: deno `…/problems/404`, php 422 title "Unprocessable Content", python "Unprocessable Entity", plus php's extra `detail`. This is allowed, but it fingerprints the backend. | nit | yes |
| 19 | node-ts, deno, python | 100 KB header; `Authorization: Bearer tok_alice\x01`; `/notes/é` (raw non-ASCII) | NOTES-TECH-ERR-1: every 4xx is problem+json | node and deno return a bare 400 or 431 with no body. python returns a 431 **text/html** page. php closes the connection. | nit (transport layer) | yes |
| 20 | deno | 2 MiB + 10 bytes POST, then a pipelined GET on the same socket | After `Connection: close`, stop | deno sends `Connection: close` and then still serves the pipelined GET (200) | nit | yes |
| 21 | all | `HEAD /notes/{id}` and `HEAD /me` as alice | Not in the spec | 404 everywhere (ADR-0003: unknown method gets 404). Consistent. | nit | no |

# Team Notes red-team findings (2026-10-26, 15:53–15:59 CDT)

Black-box HTTP probes against the four backends, aimed by reading the source. Ports: 4201 node-ts, 4202 deno, 4203 php, 4204 python. Each backend used a throwaway DB under `/tmp` (`/tmp/rt-*.db`). No repo files were changed.

Scripts in this directory:
- `probe.mjs` is the raw-socket sweep (paths, headers, JSON, If-Match, leaks, framing). Its output is in `results.txt`, and `compare.mjs` writes the side-by-side view to `compare.txt`.
- `probe2.mjs` covers persistence, 20-way races, pipelining and timing (`results2.txt`). `timing.mjs` is the 1,500-sample timing run (`timing.txt`).
- `size.sh` covers the 2 MiB boundary, `deno-nul.sh` the NUL truncation, and `rawsend.mjs` is a raw TCP sender.
- `repro.sh` re-runs every top finding as an exact curl or raw request. Its output is in `repro.txt`.

Severity: **blocker** breaks a ratified card or loses data, **should-fix** is a real defect or a spec gap that lets backends diverge, and **nit** is cosmetic or low impact.

## Findings

| # | Backend | Probe (exact) | Expected per spec | Actual | Severity | Differs across backends? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | node-ts, deno | `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_alice' localhost:PORT/notes/%E0` (also `%C0%AE`, `/notes/%`, `/teams/%E0/notes`, PATCH, DELETE, `POST /notes/%E0/restore`) | 404, byte-identical to the 404 for a random UUID (NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3, malformed id) | **500** problem+json. `decodeURIComponent` throws on an invalid escape (node `http.ts:78`, deno `http.ts:89,104`). | **blocker** | yes: php and python return 404 |
| 1b | node-ts | `curl localhost:4201/notes/%E0` (no token) | 401 (401 comes first in NOTES-TECH-ERR-2) | **500**. Path decoding runs before authentication. | **blocker** | yes: deno, php and python return 401 |
| 2 | deno | `./deno-nul.sh 4202`: POST `{"title":"\u0000","body":"keep\u0000secret-tail"}` | 201 storing the strings as sent (as node, php and python do), or 422 | 201, then GET returns `"title":""` and `"body":"keep"`. Everything after U+0000 is **silently truncated**, so an empty title (minLength 1) gets persisted. The list responses then break NOTES-TECH-CONTRACT-1. | **blocker** (data loss and contract violation) | yes |
| 3 | node-ts, deno | `printf '{"title":"a\xff\xfe"}' \| curl -X POST .../teams/team-red/notes -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @-` and `-d '{"title":"\ud800x"}'` | 400, because invalid UTF-8 is malformed JSON (RFC 8259). At minimum the stored value must match the response. | 201. Invalid bytes are replaced with U+FFFD and stored. For a lone surrogate, **node's 201 body says `"\ud800x"` but a later GET returns `"�x"`**, under the same ETag `"1"`. | should-fix | yes: php 400/400, python 400/422 |
| 4 | all | PATCH with `If-Match: "1", "2"`, `If-Match: "1", *` or `If-Match: "01"` on a v1 note, and duplicate `If-Match` headers (`"9"` then `"1"`) | Not pinned beyond "missing or `*` gets 428, stale gets 412" (NOTES-FUNC-CONC-2/3). RFC 9110 says a list matches if any member matches, and the strong comparison is octet-exact, so `"01"` ≠ `"1"`. | **node**: every list gets 412, and `"01"` gets **200** (the regex is numeric). **deno, php**: `"1", *` gets 200 and duplicate headers are joined. **python**: `"1", *` gets 428, and for duplicate headers the first one wins (412). | should-fix (add an AC card) | yes, four different behaviors |
| 5 | deno (php weaker) | `node timing.mjs 4202`: carol GETs alice's note (99 KB body), a random UUID and `zz`, 1,500 samples each in random order | No existence leak through status, body, headers **or timing** (ADR-0001) | deno: hidden p25 108 µs / p50 137 µs vs random 79 / 101 µs, so a non-member's 404 is about **30 µs slower** when the note exists. `findNote` loads the whole row and then `isMember` runs. php: about 25 µs slower (710 vs 687 µs). node-ts: no gap (it uses one JOIN). Python's 40 ms keep-alive delay (#7) hides any gap. | should-fix | yes |
| 6 | python | `printf 'GET /health HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: -1\r\n\r\n' \| node rawsend.mjs 4204 3000` | 400 | **Hangs**. `rfile.read(-1)` blocks the worker thread until the client closes, so one client can pin unbounded threads. `Content-Length: abc` or `1e1` closes the connection with no response. | should-fix (DoS) | yes: node and deno answer 400 |
| 6b | python | chunked body with size line `zz` (see `repro.sh` F14) | 400 | **500** (`int('zz',16)` raises ValueError) | should-fix | yes: node 400, deno and php drop the connection |
| 6c | python, php | `Content-Length: 13` and `Content-Length: 14` (python), or `Content-Length: 4` plus `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (python and php) | 400. RFC 9112 forbids these, and they enable request smuggling behind a proxy. | 201. Python uses the first CL or the chunked body, php the chunked body. | should-fix | yes: node and deno answer 400 |
| 7 | python | `curl -s -o /dev/null -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' localhost:4204/health localhost:4204/health` | Comparable latency | First request 1.7 ms, then **40 ms per request** on a keep-alive connection. Headers and body go out in separate small writes, so Nagle's algorithm meets delayed ACKs. Every keep-alive client (fetch/undici, browsers) pays this. | should-fix (perf) | yes |
| 8 | php | `printf 'GET /health ...\r\n\r\nGET /health ...\r\n\r\n' \| node rawsend.mjs 4203 3000` | Two responses (or one plus `Connection: close`) | **No response at all**: pipelined requests are dropped by `php -S`. Malformed framing (`CL: abc`, `-1`, a path without a leading slash) also closes with no response, and duplicate CL hangs for more than 4 s. | should-fix (`php -S` is a dev server) | yes |
| 9 | node-ts | `curl localhost:4201/nope`, `curl -I localhost:4201/health`, `OPTIONS *` (no token) | NOTES-SEC-AUTHN-1 binds "all paths except `GET /health`", so 401. ADR-0003 says an unknown route gets the same 404 as a missing one. The two rules conflict for unauthenticated requests. | node: **404** (route check before auth), and `GET /health/` returns 200. Others: 401. | should-fix (pin in an AC) | yes |
| 10 | node-ts, deno vs php, python | `curl -X POST .../teams/team-red/notes -H "$A"` (no body, no Content-Type). `PATCH` with `Content-Type: text/plain` and `Content-Length: 0`. | NOTES-TECH-ERR-2: 415 only when "a body is sent". With no body the request is malformed, so 400. | node: 415 in both cases. deno: 415 for the first and 400 for the second. php and python: 400 in both. | should-fix | yes |
| 11 | all | Title made only of `\u001f`, `\u0085`, `\u180e` or `\ufeff` | "Trimmed" (NOTES-TECH-FMT-1) with one definition across backends (ADR-0003) | U+001F: python trims (422), the rest store it. U+0085: php and python trim (422), node and deno store it. U+180E: only php trims. U+FEFF: python **stores a BOM-only title**, the rest trim it (422). | should-fix (pin the whitespace set) | yes |
| 12 | all | `GET /teams/team-red/notes?archived=true&archived=false` and the reverse order | One defined behavior | node and deno use the first value, php and python the last, so the same URL returns trash on two backends and live notes on the other two. | nit | yes |
| 13 | all | `/teams/team-red/notes/`, `/me/`, `/notes/{id}/`, `/teams/team%2Dred/notes`, `/x/../me`, `/x/%2e%2e/me`, `//me` | Exact paths only (OpenAPI) | Trailing slash: node and php return 200, deno and python 404 (`/me/` and `/teams/` return 200 only on node). `%2D` gets 404 on python, which never percent-decodes, and 200 elsewhere. Dot segments: node and deno resolve them to 200. `//me` and `//teams/team-red/notes` return 200 only on python. | nit | yes |
| 14 | python, php | `{"title":99…9}` (5,000 digits). `{"title":"x","z":[[[…600 deep…]]]}`. `{"title":"x","\u0000a":1}`. | 422, because the JSON is well-formed but invalid | python returns **400** for the huge int (int max-str-digits limit). php returns **400** for nesting deeper than 512 and for a NUL-prefixed key. | nit | yes |
| 15 | deno | POST with a UTF-8 BOM before `{"title":"x"}` | 400 (malformed JSON, as on the other three) | 201 (TextDecoder strips the BOM) | nit | yes |
| 16 | all | `GET /me` with two `Authorization` headers (carol's, then alice's) | 401, or one defined behavior | node and python authenticate as the **first** token (carol). deno and php return 401. | nit | yes |
| 17 | php, python | Response headers on any request; `DELETE` 204 | No version disclosure; a 204 has no Content-Type | php sends `X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.12` and `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8` on the 204. python sends `Server: TeamNotesPy Python/3.14.8`. | nit | yes |
| 18 | all | Any 404/422 compared across backends | Problem bodies are pinned only within a backend (NOTES-SEC-AUTHZ-3) | `type` and `title` differ by backend: deno `…/problems/404`, php 422 title "Unprocessable Content", python "Unprocessable Entity", plus php's extra `detail`. This is allowed, but it fingerprints the backend. | nit | yes |
| 19 | node-ts, deno, python | 100 KB header; `Authorization: Bearer tok_alice\x01`; `/notes/é` (raw non-ASCII) | NOTES-TECH-ERR-1: every 4xx is problem+json | node and deno return a bare 400 or 431 with no body. python returns a 431 **text/html** page. php closes the connection. | nit (transport layer) | yes |
| 20 | deno | 2 MiB + 10 bytes POST, then a pipelined GET on the same socket | After `Connection: close`, stop | deno sends `Connection: close` and then still serves the pipelined GET (200) | nit | yes |
| 21 | all | `HEAD /notes/{id}` and `HEAD /me` as alice | Not in the spec | 404 everywhere (ADR-0003: unknown method gets 404). Consistent. | nit | no |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Export this Claude Code session's transcript and every subagent's transcript into docs/transcripts/,
# with secrets redacted (GitHub tokens, the dogfood tokens, bearer tokens other than the documented dev tokens).
#   scripts/export-transcripts.sh <session-id>
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
SID=${1:?session id}
SRC=~/.claude/projects/-home-user-Projects-project
OUT=docs/transcripts; mkdir -p "$OUT/subagents"
redact() {
  # Order matters: specific secrets first, then generic token shapes. The dev tokens tok_alice/bob/carol are public by design.
  local extra=""
  [[ -f .dogfood/tokens ]] && extra=$(cut -d= -f2 .dogfood/tokens | paste -sd'|')
  sed -E \
    -e 's/(gh[opsu]_)[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/\1REDACTED/g' \
    -e 's/(github_pat_)[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}/\1REDACTED/g' \
    -e 's/(sk-ant-[a-z0-9-]*)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/\1REDACTED/g' \
    -e 's/(AKIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}/\1REDACTED/g' \
    ${extra:+-e "s/($extra)/tok_REDACTED/g"}
}
redact < "$SRC/$SID.jsonl" > "$OUT/main-session.jsonl"
for f in "$SRC/$SID"/subagents/*; do redact < "$f" > "$OUT/subagents/$(basename "$f")"; done
# Post-check: fail loudly if anything token-shaped survived.
if grep -rEq 'gh[opsu]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}|sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,}' "$OUT"; then
  echo "secret-shaped string survived redaction" >&2; exit 1; fi
ls "$OUT/subagents" | wc -l | xargs echo "subagent transcripts:"
du -sh "$OUT"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/export-transcripts.sh && ls ~/.claude/projects/-home-user-Projects-project/05669a8b-318d-49ce-bb3a-49c246302fda/subagents | head -3; grep -cE 'gh[opsu]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}' ~/.claude/projects/-home-user-Projects-project/05669a8b-318d-49ce-bb3a-49c246302fda.jsonl

Base directory for this skill: <tmp>/bundled-skills/2.1.310/e223ca1dfbd60d4235a33f4f99d91d10/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

content.thinking: Found the real issue: the fault check was reusing port 3101 and hitting a leftover server from the official run instead of its own build. Fixing it by making both scripts refuse to start on an in-use port and giving the fault check its own dedicated port.

input.command:
ss -ltnp | grep -E ':31[0-9][0-9] ' | head; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='scripts/falsify.sh'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("PORT=3101","PORT=${FALSIFY_PORT:-3141}",1)
s=s.replace('  FAULT="$f" PORT=$PORT','  # Refuse a busy port: a stale server would answer /health and silently replace the faulty build under test.\n  if curl -sf "http://localhost:$PORT/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "ERROR: port $PORT already serving; refusing (stale server would fake results)"; exit 2; fi\n  FAULT="$f" PORT=$PORT',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='scripts/conform-all.sh'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('  start "$b" "$p" >','  if curl -sf "http://localhost:$p/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "$b: port $p already serving; refusing (stale server would fake verdicts)" >&2; status=1; continue; fi\n  start "$b" "$p" >',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n 'refusing' scripts/falsify.sh scripts/conform-all.sh | head -3; for P in $(ss -ltnp | grep -E ':31[0-9][0-9] ' | grep -o 'pid=[0-9]*' | cut -d= -f2 | sort -u); do kill $P; done; sleep 1; scripts/falsify.sh > evidence/falsify.node-ts.txt 2>&1; echo falsify=$?; cat evidence/falsify.node-ts.txt | tail -5

input.prompt:
Repo: `~/Projects/project`. Add Rust to the Docker benchmark, then run the full Docker bench across all 5 backends. Only create or edit `backends/rust/Dockerfile`, `bench/docker-compose.yml` and `evidence/bench.docker.*`. Don't edit backend source, `spec/` or `conformance/`. Don't commit or push. Time box: 20 minutes.

1. **Write `backends/rust/Dockerfile`:**
   - A multi-stage build: `rust:1` builder → `debian:bookworm-slim` runtime.
   - The build context is the repo root, because the crate reads `spec/schema.sql` via `include_str!`. Check `backends/rust/src` for the exact path.
   - Cache dependencies sensibly.
   - The container listens on PORT 3000 with `DB_PATH=/data/notes.db` or `:memory:`, following the pattern in `backends/node-ts/Dockerfile` and `bench/docker-compose.yml`.
2. **Enable the `rust` service** in `bench/docker-compose.yml` on host port 4106 with the same caps (`cpus: "1.0"`, `mem_limit: 512m`).
3. **Rebuild every image**, because the other backends changed since the last Docker run: `docker compose -f bench/docker-compose.yml build`.
   - Then, for each service, run `BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port> node conformance/run.mjs --strict`. It must be **94/94**.
   - If a container fails, report it, and don't fix the backend code.
4. **Run** `bench/run-docker.sh --runs 3 --duration 4 --json evidence/bench.docker.json` across all 5 services, and copy `bench/results/latest.md` to `evidence/bench.docker.md`.
   - Also produce `evidence/bench.docker.raw.md`, a compact table with one row per backend and these raw values: req/s for read, list, write, mixed; contention ok-writes/s; and p99 ms for read and write. Plus the composite score.

Use docker compose down at the end. Never use `pkill -f`.

**Report back** in under 150 words: conformance per container, the composite scores, and the raw table.

Rebuild the Team Notes REST service in **C# / .NET 9, ASP.NET Core minimal API + Microsoft.Data.Sqlite**, working only from the spec. This is part of an experiment in whether the spec, the ratified ACs and the conformance suite are enough to rebuild in a new language quickly. **The .NET SDK is NOT installed locally, so build and run everything in Docker** (`mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0` to build, `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:9.0` to run).

**Rules:**
- **Allowed reading:** `spec/` (openapi.yaml, acceptance-criteria.md, schema.sql), `conformance/` (cases.json, run.mjs), `docs/adr/`, `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`.
- **Forbidden:** reading anything under `backends/` except your own folder.
- **Don't edit:** `spec/` or `conformance/`.
- **Scope:** every ratified card (tiers 1, 2, 2.1 and 3, and FMT-3/AUTHN-3).

**Read these carefully:**
- the error order: 401→404→403→415→413→400→422→409→428→412
- identical 404 bytes
- If-Match RFC 9110 strong-list semantics
- the uniform 415 rule
- I-JSON (lone surrogates and invalid UTF-8 → 400)
- code-point lengths with Unicode White_Space trimming
- teams and membership
- the 16-way concurrency case (use a single conditional UPDATE)

- a `Dockerfile` with the build context at the repo root, copying `spec/` so `schema.sql` can be loaded; it listens on PORT 3000 and takes `DB_PATH`

- unit tests, if feasible in the time
- `README.md` and `BUILD_NOTES.md`

Agreed. The new implementations are for finding edge cases. The submission's showcase should be a head-to-head of the top three, with tests and benchmarks as the differentiator. Here's how I'll pick and present them:

- **Selection is by evidence, not preference:** correctness gates (94/94, 0 invariant violations, 0 lost updates) first, then the Docker benchmark score, then test depth (mutation score, unit tests, deliberate-fault checks). My guess is Node/TS (the reference, with the most test depth) plus Rust and Deno. The Docker run including Rust decides it.
- **Comparison file (`evidence/top3.md`), one row per implementation:**
  - correctness: conformance, red-team fuzzer, deliberate faults caught
  - test strength: unit tests, mutation score from Uncle Bob's `mutator`, survivors
  - performance: raw requests/s and p99 per scenario, capped at 1 CPU / 512 MB, mean ± spread over 3 runs

content.text: Most of the agent's Host-header workarounds come from a defect in my test runner, not in the backends. Its raw-request mode sent no `Host` header, which HTTP/1.1 requires, so rejecting those requests was correct behavior. The runner now sends `Host`. The backend workarounds are harmless, and Bun's move to `node:http` is still needed for the separate dot-segment issue. Merging, fixing the runner, then running Gate 4 across all nine:

input.command:
git merge --no-ff -q worktree-agent-ade6a20b99afbdb5e -m "Merge AUTHN-4 for bun/dotnet/go/java (97/97 each)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && chmod +x backends/*/run.sh && sed -i "s|  const flat = \[...Object.entries(headers).flat(), ...pairs.flat()\];|  // HTTP/1.1 requires Host (RFC 9112 §3.2). Its absence was a runner bug that backends had to work around.\n  const flat = ['Host', u.host, ...Object.entries(headers).flat(), ...pairs.flat()];|" conformance/run.mjs && grep -n "'Host', u.host" conformance/run.mjs && git add -A backends conformance/run.mjs && git commit -qm "Runner: raw requests send Host (RFC 9112); run.sh files executable

Why: Kestrel, Go net/http and Bun rejected the runner's Host-less raw
requests with 400. That was correct HTTP/1.1 behavior and a runner bug. The
backend workarounds stay (harmless), but the suite no longer requires them.

- Alias, linked to its heading in `spec/acceptance-criteria.md` (GitHub anchor)
- One-line claim, at most 15 words
- Cases, the count from `cases.json`

# How the service works

Team Notes is a REST API for notes shared within small teams. The contract is [`spec/openapi.yaml`](../spec/openapi.yaml), with a rendered reference at [`docs/api.html`](api.html). The rules it must follow are in [`spec/acceptance-criteria.md`](../spec/acceptance-criteria.md).

## Data model

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ MEMBERSHIP : has
  TEAM ||--o{ MEMBERSHIP : has
  TEAM ||--o{ NOTE : owns
  USER ||--o{ NOTE : wrote
  MEMBERSHIP { string role "owner or member" }
  NOTE { uuid id  string title  string body  int version  time deletedAt }
```

- **Notes:** a note belongs to one team. Every member of that team can read and edit it, and its author is kept.
- **Versions:** every change increments `version` by one.
- **Storage:** all nine backends share one SQLite schema, [`spec/schema.sql`](../spec/schema.sql).

## Visibility

If you can't see something, you get a 404, and the 404 body is byte-for-byte the same in every one of these cases:
- a note in a team you aren't in
- an id that never existed
- a malformed id
- a deleted note
- an unknown route

Probing ids tells an outsider nothing.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| Anything except `/health`, without a valid token | 401 |
| Another team's note, a random id, `/notes/%E0`, `/notes/{id}/` | 404, identical bytes |
| A team member who is not the owner changes membership | 403, because they can already see the team |

## Concurrent edits

Every single-note response carries `ETag: "<version>"`. To update a note, send that value back in `If-Match`:
- **Atomic:** the server checks and increments in one statement, `UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`.
- **Stale copy:** if someone else changed the note first, you get **412** along with the current ETag.
- **No precondition:** with no `If-Match`, or `If-Match: *`, you get **428**. There are no blind overwrites.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Alice
  participant S as Server
  participant B as Bob
  A->>S: GET /notes/42
  S-->>A: 200, ETag "1"
  B->>S: GET /notes/42
  S-->>B: 200, ETag "1"
  A->>S: PATCH, If-Match "1"
  S-->>A: 200, ETag "2"
  B->>S: PATCH, If-Match "1"
  S-->>B: 412, ETag "2"
```

The suite checks this sequentially, and also fires 16 simultaneous PATCHes at one note and requires exactly one to succeed.

## Delete and restore

- **Delete:** `DELETE` sets `deletedAt` and keeps the content. Repeating it returns 204 again, and it does not change `version`.
- **Restore:** `POST /notes/{id}/restore` brings the note back and increments `version`, so anyone still holding a version from before the delete gets 412.
- **Trash:** `GET /teams/{id}/notes?archived=true` lists a team's deleted notes.

## Teams

- **Creating:** anyone can create a team (`POST /teams` with a slug id) and becomes its owner.
- **Membership:** only the owner adds or removes members. Access changes on the next request: a removed member gets 404, even for notes they wrote.
- **Notes stay:** those notes remain with the team.
- **Last owner:** the last owner can't be removed (409).

## Errors

Every error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` document. When a request has several problems, the first one in this order is reported, in every backend:

**401 → 404 → 403 → 415 → 413 → 400 → 422 → 409 → 428 → 412**

That's authentication, then visibility, then permission, then the body (media type, size, JSON syntax, field validation), then state (conflict, then the version precondition). A caller who isn't allowed learns nothing about their request body.

Request bodies must be valid JSON with valid Unicode (I-JSON, RFC 7493). Titles are trimmed of Unicode whitespace and limited to 200 code points. Bodies are limited to 100,000 code points.

## Implementations

| Backend | Stack | Runtime dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| node-ts | Node 26, node:http, node:sqlite | none |
| deno | Deno 2.9, Deno.serve, node:sqlite | none |
| bun | Bun, node:http, bun:sqlite | none |
| python | standard-library http.server, sqlite3 | none |
| php | PHP 8.5 built-in server, PDO SQLite | none |
| rust | axum, rusqlite | 10 crates |
| go | net/http, modernc.org/sqlite | 1 module |
| java | JDK HttpServer, sqlite-jdbc | 2 |
| dotnet | ASP.NET Core minimal API, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite | 1 |

Each one passes the same conformance suite. See [`evidence/matrix.md`](../evidence/matrix.md).

# How the service works

Team Notes is a REST API for notes shared within small teams. The contract is [`spec/openapi.yaml`](../spec/openapi.yaml), with a rendered reference at [`docs/api.html`](api.html). The rules it must follow are in [`spec/acceptance-criteria.md`](../spec/acceptance-criteria.md).

## Data model

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ MEMBERSHIP : has
  TEAM ||--o{ MEMBERSHIP : has
  TEAM ||--o{ NOTE : owns
  USER ||--o{ NOTE : wrote
  MEMBERSHIP { string role "owner or member" }
  NOTE { uuid id  string title  string body  int version  time deletedAt }
```

- **Notes:** a note belongs to one team. Every member of that team can read and edit it, and its author is kept.
- **Versions:** every change increments `version` by one.
- **Storage:** all nine backends share one SQLite schema, [`spec/schema.sql`](../spec/schema.sql).

## Visibility

If you can't see something, you get a 404, and the 404 body is byte-for-byte the same in every one of these cases:
- a note in a team you aren't in
- an id that never existed
- a malformed id
- a deleted note
- an unknown route

Probing ids tells an outsider nothing.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| Anything except `/health`, without a valid token | 401 |
| Another team's note, a random id, `/notes/%E0`, `/notes/{id}/` | 404, identical bytes |
| A team member who is not the owner changes membership | 403, because they can already see the team |

## Concurrent edits

Every single-note response carries `ETag: "<version>"`. To update a note, send that value back in `If-Match`:
- **Atomic:** the server checks and increments in one statement, `UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`.
- **Stale copy:** if someone else changed the note first, you get **412** along with the current ETag.
- **No precondition:** with no `If-Match`, or `If-Match: *`, you get **428**. There are no blind overwrites.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Alice
  participant S as Server
  participant B as Bob
  A->>S: GET /notes/42
  S-->>A: 200, ETag "1"
  B->>S: GET /notes/42
  S-->>B: 200, ETag "1"
  A->>S: PATCH, If-Match "1"
  S-->>A: 200, ETag "2"
  B->>S: PATCH, If-Match "1"
  S-->>B: 412, ETag "2"
```

The suite checks this sequentially, and also fires 16 simultaneous PATCHes at one note and requires exactly one to succeed.

## Delete and restore

- **Delete:** `DELETE` sets `deletedAt` and keeps the content. Repeating it returns 204 again, and it does not change `version`.
- **Restore:** `POST /notes/{id}/restore` brings the note back and increments `version`, so anyone still holding a version from before the delete gets 412.
- **Trash:** `GET /teams/{id}/notes?archived=true` lists a team's deleted notes.

Nothing broken, but there are real gaps a sharp reviewer will spot. Rough priority:

**Obvious omissions**
1. **No CI.** Nothing runs the suite on push. This is the most visible one for a "proof" repo. A GitHub Actions workflow for Node/Deno/Python/PHP/Rust plus the conformance suite takes about 10 minutes and is low risk.
2. **List endpoints are unbounded.** There's no pagination (Tier 3 cut it), so one team's list can grow without limit. That's both a performance and a DoS concern, and the benchmark already shows lists slowing as notes pile up.
3. **The suite isn't safe to re-run on a used database.** `teams-carol-only-blue` expects exactly `[team-blue]`, but another case makes Carol create a team. The .NET and Java agents both hit this. It's a test-isolation flaw, and a one-line fix.
4. **No LICENSE file.** Without one, a public repo is "all rights reserved" by default.

**Security, stated honestly**
- **CORS:** none, on purpose. Browsers block cross-origin calls by default, which is the safe default for an API with no web client. It just needs to be written down: "add an allowlist when a browser client exists."
- **Auth:** static seeded tokens with unsalted SHA-256 hashes, no expiry, no rate limiting or lockout. Fine for a dev harness, but it needs a clear "not production auth" note.
- **SQL injection:** probably fine, but **not verified across all nine backends**. A 2-minute grep for string-built SQL would turn that into a fact.
- **Python and PHP run on development servers.** Grok found request-smuggling-shaped framing issues (conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding) and a ~30 µs timing difference on hidden notes in Deno and PHP. These should be listed as known gaps.
- **Not done:** dependency audits (`npm audit`, `cargo audit`), and Docker images run as root.

**Incomplete work**
- Go, Java, .NET and Bun aren't benchmarked yet. That's queued after the final run finishes.
- .NET has no unit tests.
- Grok's PR #73 (Tier 3 race cases) is still unresolved.
- The Node mutation score comes from an earlier version of its domain code.

mkdir -p .github/workflows && cat > .github/workflows/conformance.yml <<'EOF'
name: conformance
# On every push and PR: run each locally-toolchained backend's unit tests,
# then the language-neutral conformance suite against it (--strict: every ratified AC needs a passing case).
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check-cases:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '26' }
      - run: cd conformance && npm ci
      - run: node conformance/run.mjs --check
  backend:
    needs: check-cases
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        backend: [node-ts, deno, python, php, rust]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '26' }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'deno'
        uses: denoland/setup-deno@v2
        with: { deno-version: v2.x }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'python'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.14' }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'php'
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@v2
        with: { php-version: '8.4', extensions: pdo_sqlite, mbstring }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'rust'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - run: cd conformance && npm ci
      - name: unit tests
        run: |
          case ${{ matrix.backend }} in
            node-ts) cd backends/node-ts && npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck ;;
            deno)    cd backends/deno && deno task test ;;
            python)  python3 -m unittest discover -s backends/python/tests ;;
            php)     php backends/php/tests/run.php ;;
            rust)    cd backends/rust && cargo test --release ;;
          esac
      - name: conformance (--strict)
        run: |
          if [ ${{ matrix.backend }} = node-ts ]; then (cd backends/node-ts && PORT=3001 node src/server.ts &) ;
          elif [ ${{ matrix.backend }} = php ]; then PORT=3001 DB_PATH=$RUNNER_TEMP/notes.db backends/php/run.sh &

name: conformance
# On every push and PR: run each locally-toolchained backend's unit tests,
# then the language-neutral conformance suite against it (--strict: every ratified AC needs a passing case).
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check-cases:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '26' }
      - run: cd conformance && npm ci
      - run: node conformance/run.mjs --check
  backend:
    needs: check-cases
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        backend: [node-ts, deno, python, php, rust]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '26' }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'deno'
        uses: denoland/setup-deno@v2
        with: { deno-version: v2.x }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'python'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.14' }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'php'
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@v2
        with: { php-version: '8.4', extensions: pdo_sqlite, mbstring }
      - if: matrix.backend == 'rust'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - run: cd conformance && npm ci
      - name: unit tests
        run: |
          case ${{ matrix.backend }} in
            node-ts) cd backends/node-ts && npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck ;;
            deno)    cd backends/deno && deno task test ;;
            python)  python3 -m unittest discover -s backends/python/tests ;;
            php)     php backends/php/tests/run.php ;;
            rust)    cd backends/rust && cargo test --release ;;
          esac
      - name: conformance (--strict)
        run: |
          if [ ${{ matrix.backend }} = node-ts ]; then (cd backends/node-ts && PORT=3001 node src/server.ts &) ;
          elif [ ${{ matrix.backend }} = php ]; then PORT=3001 DB_PATH=$RUNNER_TEMP/notes.db backends/php/run.sh &

          for i in $(seq 300); do curl -sf localhost:3001/health && break; sleep 1; done

EOF

A card in `spec/acceptance-criteria.md` has a Claim, a Forbids list and a Falsifier. The Falsifier is a concrete test that would refute the Claim. A case in `conformance/cases.json` points at a card with `"falsifies": "<alias>"`, so a failing case means the card does not hold for that backend. # Team Notes

[![conformance](https://github.com/CoeusCC/team-notes-polyglot/actions/workflows/conformance.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/CoeusCC/team-notes-polyglot/actions/workflows/conformance.yml)

A notes API for small teams. It has one written contract and nine implementations, and all nine pass one shared test suite.
Read the [design choices](#design-choices) below, or run it with the two commands in the next section.
Evidence and the full story are in the [proof ledger](https://coeuscc.github.io/team-notes-polyglot/explainer/proof.html).

## Run it

Requires Node 26 or newer. The reference backend has no runtime dependencies.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/CoeusCC/team-notes-polyglot && cd team-notes-polyglot
cd backends/node-ts && npm install && npm start            # API on http://localhost:3001
```

In a second shell, from the repo root:

```bash
scripts/demo.sh                                            # guided curl walkthrough
(cd conformance && npm install) && node conformance/run.mjs --strict   # all 97 cases
```

The demo users have dev tokens `tok_alice` (owner of team-red), `tok_bob` (member of team-red) and `tok_carol` (owner of team-blue). The other backends start with `backends/<name>/run.sh`. To test every backend, run `scripts/conform-all.sh`.

| Read next | |
|---|---|
| [docs/SERVICE.md](docs/SERVICE.md) | How the API behaves: visibility, concurrent edits, delete and restore, teams, errors |
| [API reference](https://coeuscc.github.io/team-notes-polyglot/api.html) | Rendered from [`spec/openapi.yaml`](spec/openapi.yaml) |
| [docs/ACCEPTANCE.md](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md) | Every acceptance rule in one table, and how three of them got sharper |
| [START-HERE.md](START-HERE.md) | A guided tour of the repo |

## Design choices

### 1. Write the rules first, then let any language implement them
- **Decision:** the API is defined by an OpenAPI file plus 40 acceptance rules. A person approved each rule, and each one names the test that would prove it false. 97 language-neutral HTTP test cases check those rules against any backend.
- **Gave up:** time spent writing rules before code.
- **Why:** it made rebuilding cheap and checkable. Independent agents rebuilt the service in seven other languages from the rules alone, and each passed the suite on its first run. Where green backends still behaved differently, we tightened the rules ([examples](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md#how-cards-got-sharper)).

### 2. No lost edits, and no leaks between teams
- **Decision:** every note carries a version. An edit must send the version it read (`If-Match`). If someone else saved first, the edit gets 412 instead of overwriting. Anything outside your teams returns the same 404 bytes as something that doesn't exist.
- **Gave up:** a little client convenience: clients must re-read and retry, and they get no "forbidden" hint.
- **Why:** concurrent editing is the main risk in a shared notes app. A test fires 16 edits at once and requires exactly one to win.

### 3. Plain tables and soft delete, not event sourcing
- **Decision:** we store current state with a version column. Delete only marks a note, and restore brings it back.
- **Gave up:** full edit history and an event stream for other systems.
- **Why:** event sourcing would multiply the code and behavior to specify in every language. The upgrade path is an outbox that emits CloudEvents ([ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-architecture.md)).

The reasoning behind each decision is recorded in [docs/adr/](docs/adr/), with one short "in the context of… we decided… accepting…" statement per decision.

## What I'd change with more time
- **Add:** pagination (the `seq` column is already in place), tags and search, ownership transfer, and real auth (OIDC) instead of seeded tokens.
- **Add:** rate limiting, security headers, and benchmarks for every backend under production servers.
- **Change:** report core rules and environment-specific rules separately in the test runner. Add hidden test cases that implementers never see, to catch overfitting.
- **Stop:** using the Python and PHP development servers for anything except proving the contract.

## Security
- **CORS:** none, on purpose. This is a server-to-server API; a browser client would go through a same-origin gateway or an allow-list.
- **Auth:** seeded dev tokens, stored as SHA-256 hashes. There's no expiry, rotation or signup. Not production auth.
- **Isolation:** team membership is checked in SQL. Tests and a fuzzer confirm that nothing leaks across teams.
- **SQL injection:** every backend uses parameterized queries. An audit found only constant SQL fragments.
- **Input limits:** 2 MiB bodies, valid UTF-8 JSON only, and limits of 200 and 100,000 characters on title and body.
- **Not done:** pagination, rate limiting, security headers, dependency audits, and non-root containers.
- **Known issues:** listed in the [proof ledger](https://coeuscc.github.io/team-notes-polyglot/explainer/proof.html#gaps).

## How it was built
- **Patrick** set the goals, approved every rule and made the design calls. He also overruled the agent where it mattered.
- **Claude Code** wrote the spec and tests and coordinated the work. **Claude Sonnet** agents built the backends.
- **Grok** reviewed adversarially and built three more replications.

Each gate is logged in [`docs/build-digest.md`](docs/build-digest.md). The full chat logs are in [`docs/transcripts/`](docs/transcripts/). MIT licensed.
